clue.text: Perhaps skip politician being entertained by cleaner

indicators.note: the politician is a guest held within the cleaner, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a duster is a cloth for cleaning
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician gets a lift from a cleaner, maybe in a skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British word for a large open waste container left on a street or building site.
explanation.definitionFit: A British skip is an example of a large rubbish container, which Americans call by this trade name; 'Perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Significant destruction in December: excitement a November missed

parts.note: DEC, December

indicators.note: left out, so the letters for 'a November' are dropped

parts.note: animation is liveliness, excitement
A plus N, November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A December of great destruction, the excitement of November gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' takes A and N out of ANIMATION, leaving IMATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the Roman killing of one soldier in ten, it now means the wiping out of a large proportion.

clue.text: A few programmes, fashionable, probing wretched conditions

indicators.note: the fashionable letters probe into, and so sit inside, the wretched conditions

parts.note: miseries are states of wretchedness
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A short run of trendy documentaries investigating squalid living conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A short serial of television episodes telling one story is a few programmes made as a set.

clue.text: Government blocking paintings going up in Irish town

indicators.note: the government letter stands in the middle, blocking the way
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: oils are oil paintings
G, government

explanation.surface: The government obstructs paintings being hung in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns OILS into SLIO; G goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland, a straightforward example.

clue.text: Endless interest Queen developed as a horsewoman

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new form
without its end, so the last letter of interest goes

explanation.surface: The Queen's endless interest grew into riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the T from INTEREST, and 'developed' mixes INTERES with QUEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rider, especially one performing in a circus, is a horsewoman by the feminine French-style form.

clue.text: Counter, basic stuff, American, that has engaged one

indicators.note: the basic stuff takes on, or engages, the one, holding it inside

parts.note: ABC means the basics, as in the ABC of a subject
A as in a single thing
US, United States

explanation.surface: A list of an American counter's features, read like a product description.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for counting is literally a counter, a device for reckoning numbers.

clue.text: Attack main area of London

parts.note: to batter is to attack with repeated blows
the main is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: An instruction to assault the principal district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERSEA is a district of south-west London, home to a famous power station and dogs' home.
explanation.definitionFit: This riverside district south of the Thames is an example of a London area.

clue.text: U-turn after quantities of meat seen in Chinese dish

indicators.note: the turn comes after the meat, so it is placed second

parts.note: cuts of pork or lamb on the bone, in the plural
a 'uey' is Australian and British slang for a U-turn

explanation.surface: Someone turns around after spotting meat in a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This stir-fry of meat and vegetables is a Chinese-American dish, so an example of Chinese food.

clue.text: See 7
"Money" (you texted) "invested in ice-cream? Keep at it"

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream served in a wafer
tin is slang for money
in text messages 'you' is written U

explanation.surface: Quoted fragments of a chatty message urging someone to keep putting money into ice-cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at it is to carry on or persist, the imperative of the verb meaning to go on.

clue.text: Last of jokes also recalled for one comedy partner

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word jokes is wanted

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: called back, so the abbreviation for 'for one' is read in reverse

parts.note: EG, for example

explanation.surface: The final joke is also remembered, as one comedy double act member might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns EG (for example, i.e. 'for one') into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The straight man of a double act, who sets up the jokes and takes the blows, is the classic stooge.

clue.text: No patterns in rocks across the river?

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A geologist notes that the rocks over the river show no patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means on the far side of a bridge, especially the south side of the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally 'beyond the bridge', it describes the other side of a river, chiefly south London as seen from the north.

clue.text: Wrongly interpret consumerist moves

indicators.note: the letters of the word consumerist are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: The moves of consumerists are open to being misread.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the wrong idea of what was meant is to misunderstand or misread it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Naughtily steal steel to make a patterned floor?

indicators.note: behaving badly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone mischievously pinches steel to lay a fancy floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit shapes together without gaps, as tiles in a mosaic floor do, is one way to create a patterned floor; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Supporter of chambers heading off to appear in court case

parts.note: a stand is something that supports

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is removed

parts.note: atrial means relating to the atria, the upper chambers of the heart

explanation.surface: A backer of barristers' chambers sets off to attend a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' suggests barristers' offices but means the heart's atria; 'heading off' drops A from ATRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tried in a court of law as the accused is to appear in a court case.

clue.text: Body roughly attached to regiment, ultimately

indicators.note: in the end, so only the last letter of regiment is taken

parts.note: 'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A body is loosely attached to a regiment in the end, like a recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human frame, without head or limbs, is a body in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Caught copper and superior in middle of room, turning up for stew

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the whole is read bottom to top
the caught, copper and superior letters go inside
only the central letters of room are used

parts.note: C, caught in cricket scoring
Cu, the chemical symbol for copper
a boss is one's superior at work

explanation.surface: A policeman is caught with his boss in a room, then a stew turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives OO from ROOM; C, CU and BOSS go 'in' it, and 'turning up' reverses OCCUBOSSO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Milanese dish of braised veal shanks is an example of a stew.

clue.text: Making a comeback near broken-down trail

indicators.note: the word near is broken into pieces and reassembled

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: Someone close to a dilapidated path is staging a return.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being reborn or reviving is making a comeback; the word comes from Latin for being born again.

clue.text: Stay out having stayed out?

parts.note: to stay out overnight at a friend's house is to sleep over; reverse those two words and you have the result of having been out too late: lying in bed too long

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what follows a night spent away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Staying out is sleeping over; swap the two words round and you get what happens next morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping past the time you meant to wake is the natural consequence of a late night out.

clue.text: Fire requiring forensic study has a group of scientists working

parts.note: RS, the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of science
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A fire needs forensic study, and a team of scientists is on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberately set fire is the crime that fire investigators examine forensically.

clue.text: Mad drunk swallowing soft dessert

indicators.note: the mad and drunk words take the soft letter down inside them

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad
lit is slang for drunk
P, piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A crazed drunk wolfs down a soft pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic sweet course of a halved banana with ice cream, a dessert by example.

clue.text: English learners attending special period

parts.note: SP, special
E, English
L is the learner driver's plate, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: English learners attending a special course for a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint or short time, as in a cold snap or a turn at a job, is a period.

clue.text: Idiot taking daughter into Birmingham to get instrument

indicators.note: the idiot and daughter go into the city name

parts.note: Brum is a nickname for Birmingham, England's second city
an ass is a fool
D, daughter

explanation.surface: A fool brings his daughter into Birmingham to buy an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low-pitched drum of an orchestra or band is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: See 22
Caribbean country, discounting cost, securing fine mass of land

indicators.note: the remaining letters hold the fine letter firmly inside them
the word cost is knocked off the country's name

parts.note: Costa Rica, a Central American country with a Caribbean coast
taken as written
F, the pencil grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Reads like a bargain: a Caribbean country, discounted, obtaining a fine stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa Rica lies in Central America but has a Caribbean coastline; 'discounting' leaves ARICA, and 'securing' holds F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a great mass of land, and this is the second largest one.

clue.text: Writers etc left copy that's not acceptable

parts.note: L, left

indicators.note: the clue's 'not acceptable' means 'not on', so the letters for acceptable are removed

parts.note: an iteration is a repeated version, a copy
on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable

explanation.surface: Writers and the like produced a copy that won't do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops ON from ITERATION, leaving ITERATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The educated, literary class is a collective term for writers, critics and other well-read people.

clue.text: Request appearance of everything before start of working week

parts.note: the sum is the whole, everything
Mon, Monday, the first day of the working week

explanation.surface: Asking someone to come in before the working week begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To call or order someone to come before you is to request, or demand, their attendance.

clue.text: Impetuously supplying rhymes for 21?

definitions.meaning: in a reckless headlong rush, hastily
the two halves are each a word ending with the same sound as the answer to 21 down, so the phrase gives two rhymes for it

explanation.surface: Someone dashing off rhyming words for another entry in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: pell and mell both rhyme with the 21 down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a disorderly, headlong hurry is doing things recklessly, without care or order.
